subject.title: [Feature]: When messages are merged and processed, the agent event is expected to carry the original runId(s)

question: Should merged queued Gateway events preserve the executed runId and add an original/source run ID array, or should merged execution reuse one queued source run ID as the public runId?
rationale: Current code has enough internal queued-turn identity to design a fix, but the remaining choice changes a stable public Gateway event contract and should not be chosen by automation alone.

options.title: Add additive lineage array
options.body: Preserve the executed run identity and add a named field such as sourceRunIds or originalRunIds to public event schemas and projections.

options.title: Reuse one source ID
options.body: Use the first or last queued source run ID as the merged public run ID, simplifying simple clients but hiding multi-source lineage.

options.title: Keep current contract
options.body: Leave clients to correlate through accepted/final events and session history, accepting that merged queued execution has no live source-run lineage.

recommendation.title: Add additive lineage array
recommendation.body: Preserve the executed run identity and add a named field such as sourceRunIds or originalRunIds to public event schemas and projections.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a public Gateway protocol/event semantics choice, and steipete is the strongest current-history signal for that surface.
